RESULTS: Standard TBSS showed lower FA in the right anterior corona radiata (ACR) and posterior thalamic radiation (PTR), and higher RD in the corpus callosum genu, in MS versus HC. NAWM-restricted TBSS showed lower FA in the corpus callosum genu, right PTR, and right tapetum, and higher RD in bilateral ACR, right posterior corona radiata, and an unclassified region. In randomized, AD and MD were nonsignificant (minimum corrected p = 0.0118 and 0.0103 in standard TBSS; p = 0.0103 and 0.0107 in NAWM, respectively). Under PALM across-metric correction, no metric remained significant: standard TBSS, FA p = 0.0861, AD p = 0.1273, RD p = 0.0271, MD p = 0.0177; NAWM, FA p = 0.0807, AD p = 0.1225, RD p = 0.0282, MD p = 0.0197. CONCLUSION: Functionally defined low-disability MS shows focal WM and NAWM microstructural alterations, predominantly reflected by reduced FA and increased RD. EVIDENCE LEVEL: 4. TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 1.

articles.title: Spectrometric characterization of x-ray attenuation in silicone-gel and saline breast implants under mammography and CT conditions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Breast implants alter x-ray beam attenuation, but quantitative energy-resolved data for commercial prostheses are largely missing from the literature. Current dosimetric protocols lack specific correction factors for implant materials. PURPOSE: To measure the x-ray attenuation properties of silicone-gel (PDMS) and saline breast implants under mammography and computed tomography (CT) conditions. METHODS: We performed transmission spectrometry on six breast implants (three PDMS, three saline-filled) from a single manufacturer, using a cadmium telluride (CdTe) detector in narrow-beam geometry. Energy-dependent linear attenuation coefficients, effective attenuation coefficients ( μ eff  ), half-value layers, and bulk densities were determined for mammography (25-49 kV) and CT (80-120 kV) beam qualities. Combined uncertainties were 3%-5%. RESULTS: Under mammographic conditions, PDMS attenuates more than saline: μ eff  values are roughly 1.5-2 times higher, because of enhanced photoelectric absorption linked to a higher effective atomic number (  Z eff = 11.7  vs. 7.5). Saline implants behave much like water and soft breast tissues. The monoenergetic attenuation curves of the two materials converge above ∼ 60 keV as Compton scattering comes to dominate, but the spectrum-weighted effective attenuation still differs by ∼ 40% at a representative 80 kV Al CT tube potential (0.48 vs. 0.34  cm - 1   ), narrowing to ∼ 10% only with harder filtration and higher tube potential combined (120 kV AlCu). We provide log-log polynomial fits suitable for dosimetric codes. CONCLUSIONS: These measurements supply energy-resolved attenuation data for silicone-gel and saline implants across the diagnostic range. PDMS and saline differ substantially at mammographic energies. Their monoenergetic attenuation converges in the Compton regime, but spectrum-weighted differences persist at 80 kV and should be accounted for in breast CT dosimetry. The results are consistent with recent phantom findings on AEC response and dose variations in the presence of silicone implants.

articles.title: Monte Carlo (TOPAS) characterization of a proton therapy OBI: Automated source parameter optimization and analysis of CBCT acquisition dynamics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The cumulative radiation burden from daily cone-beam CT (CBCT) imaging is a significant concern. While Monte Carlo (MC) simulation provides the gold standard for patient-specific dosimetry, clinical implementation is hindered by the complexity of characterising proprietary X-ray source parameters. Furthermore, the dosimetric properties of the Hitachi ProBeat on-board imager (OBI), which utilizes a fixed frame rate (FFR) acquisition logic, remains uncharacterized in the literature. PURPOSE: To develop and validate a robust indirect characterization methodology that automates MC beam tuning using standard QA measurements, and to utilize this model to quantify the dosimetric impact of the Hitachi OBI's acquisition dynamics. METHODS: A TOPAS (Tool for Particle Simulation) MC model of the OBI was constructed through indirect characterization. An automated derivative-free optimization framework was developed to tune source parameters (spectrum, filtration, focal spot) by minimizing the loss against 90 static projection measurements acquired on a standard CT dose index (CTDI) phantom. A global scaling factor was used to scale simulated dose to physical dose. The model was validated against radiophotoluminescent dosimeter (RPLD) measurements in an ATOM 701 adult male anthropomorphic phantom for head and thorax protocols. Finally, the validated model was used to isolate the dosimetric overhead introduced by the system's fixed frame rate (FFR) logic compared to a theoretical fixed angular interval (FAI) acquisition. RESULTS: Optimization of beam parameters through indirect characterization successfully converged, yielding a set of simulation parameters and a general scaling factor function. In the anthropomorphic validation, the model predicted central organ doses with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 3.4%, with all in-field validation points falling within ± 10% of physical measurements. Analysis of the gantry acquisition kinematics identified up to 9.4% additional projections that were not utilized during reconstruction, and up to 23.6% additional projections compared to a theoretical FAI acquisition. Simulations indicate dose hotspots approximately 10 mGy in bone structures due to kinematic oversampling at during acceleration/deceleration phases in FFR compared to FAI acquisition. CONCLUSIONS: A high-fidelity Monte Carlo beam model can be successfully derived solely from standard CTDI measurements via automated indirect characterization, achieving a 3.4% MAPE in anthropomorphic phantom validation. This accessible framework provides a practical alternative to specialized direct beam measurements, significantly lowering the barrier to clinical implementation. Applying this tool to the Hitachi OBI quantified specific dosimetric variations inherent to its kinematic acquisition logic, identifying theoretical avenues for integral dose reduction. This facilitates the transition to accurate, patient-specific dosimetry, empowering clinics to evaluate risk-adapted IGRT strategies and better track cumulative imaging doses.

articles.title: Comparison of dose escalation strategies for head and neck cancer patients using a radiobiological model of reoxygenation.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Advanced imaging techniques for head-and-neck (HN) cancers can now quantify inter- and intra-tumor variation in tumor hypoxia. Dose-escalation based on pre-treatment hypoxia in clinical trials typically boost initial hypoxic areas. However, longitudinal studies demonstrated that the location of hypoxic cells changes throughout treatment. Our goal is to further a model of reoxygenation and quantify the potential loss of biological effectiveness due to changes in hypoxia during treatment in dose-escalation studies based on initial hypoxia only and compare this strategy to one based on patient selection according to imaging at weeks 0 and 2 of treatment and boosting of the whole treatment volume. METHODS: A published reoxygenation model based on LQ survival formulas with reoxygenation parameter Δ is extended to allow for dose-escalation with dose per fraction d H  for initial hypoxic cells. The new model allows for hypoxic cells to miss the escalated dose depending on parameter "m" (m = 0 no hypoxic cells missed). Using published radiobiological parameters, we calculate the EQD2 when hypoxia is present for 70Gy delivered in 35 fractions with  d H = 2.2 - 2.6 Gy  using two different dose escalation strategies. RESULTS: Based on assumed parameters, the increase in EQD2 associated with escalated dose per fraction up to 2.6Gy cannot sufficiently compensate for the reduction in biological effect due to hypoxia if Δ = 0  . As Δ increases to 0.2 and above the EQD2 becomes comparable to the non-hypoxic values. Based on previous results, the dose-escalation of the whole tumor after 20Gy based on hypoxia imaging at 2 weeks yields comparable or higher EQD2 values for more modest escalated doses to the whole tumor. CONCLUSIONS: The proposed reoxygenation model allows evaluation and comparison of strategies for dose-escalation to compensate for hypoxia during treatment and quantification of the limitations of dose-escalation based on the initial distribution of hypoxia in a dynamic system of tumor oxygenation.

articles.title: Scatter rejection and scatter correction for single and multiple exposure static diagnostic CT.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Static CT designs may offer several advantages, including increased compactness and mechanical simplification. In addition, acquisition speed is no longer constrained by gantry rotation but instead determined by electronic source switching and source power. Static CT further enables multiple simultaneous exposures, for example, in dual-source or even triple-source mode. Due to the static geometry, conventional anti-scatter grids (ASGs) cannot be employed, making scattered radiation a major challenge. PURPOSE: To investigate how 4th generation geometry static CTs can be made suitable for general purpose diagnostic CT imaging with regard to their scattered radiation characteristics. METHODS: In this work, we investigate how scatter can be addressed, for example, by using defocused ASGs for scatter rejection and scatter correction approaches. Our evaluation focuses not only on the correction of scatter-induced artifacts but also on the overall image quality, particularly with respect to noise degradation caused by scattered radiation. To do so, we simulate a 4th generation geometry static CT with different levels of collimation in single-source and triple-source exposure mode. It is equipped with a 360  ∘  detector ring and a 360  ∘  source ring array, eliminating the need for rotating components. For scatter rejection, we investigate the potential benefits of one-dimensional ASGs in the z-direction by comparing image quality across different ASG heights and phantom sizes. For scatter correction, we employ the deep scatter estimation (DSE), which is based on a U-Net architecture and trained with Monte Carlo-generated scatter estimates. Performance is evaluated with respect to residual scatter artifacts and noise amplification. RESULTS: DSE effectively corrects scatter artifacts in both single-source and multi-source operation, yielding reconstructions in which scatter artifacts are strongly reduced. However, in multi-source operation we observe a notable increase in image noise at constant dose levels. The use of a one-dimensional ASG in the z-direction can mitigate this noise increase and thereby enable dose savings. CONCLUSIONS: Deep learning-based methods such as DSE can effectively address scatter artifacts. However, the absence of an ASG results in increased image noise. Incorporating a one-dimensional ASG in the z-direction can reduce noise and thereby may enable dose savings.

articles.title: Letter to the Editor regarding the role of preoperative ultrasound in identifying low volume axillary disease in breast cancer.
EFM-GAN: enhanced feature modeling for multimodal MRI synthesis under missing-modality settings.
articles.abstract: Objective. Multimodal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) synthesis has been widely investigated for recovering unavailable imaging modalities under incomplete acquisition scenarios. However, existing approaches often rely on implicit feature fusion strategies, where modality-specific appearance information and cross-modal anatomical representations are entangled in a shared latent space. Such entanglement may lead to unstable feature interaction and limit the preservation of modality-invariant structural information. Moreover, although multimodal MRI sequences are generally spatially registered, modality-specific acquisition mechanisms introduce heterogeneous feature distributions, leading to feature-level semantic inconsistency during cross-modal representation learning. Lesion-related details are also frequently underrepresented, particularly in anatomically complex regions that are difficult to reconstruct.Approach. To address these limitations, an enhanced feature modeling generative adversarial network (EFM-GAN) is proposed with an explicit parallel feature modeling framework. In EFM-GAN, parallel feature branches explicitly model modality-specific appearance and cross-modal shared representations. A bidirectional progressive alignment module is further introduced to progressively reduce feature-level semantic discrepancies between modality-specific representations before feature fusion, while preserving modality-dependent appearance information. Furthermore, a reconstruction difficulty-aware loss is designed to adaptively reweight reconstruction constraints, assigning greater emphasis to regions that are harder to reconstruct.Main results. Extensive experiments on the BRaTS2020 and BRaTS2021 datasets demonstrate that EFM-GAN achieves higher peak signal-to-noise ratio and structural similarity index than the evaluated baseline methods across multiple target modalities, with improved structural consistency and synthesis fidelity.Significance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of explicitly modeling modality-specific and shared representations, progressively aligning heterogeneous features, and emphasizing reconstruction-difficult regions for missing-modality MRI synthesis.

articles.title: EDGE-Net: Enhanced Distribution Gated Eye-Vessel Network for Ophthalmic Vascular Segmentation with Topological Constraints.
articles.abstract: Ophthalmic vascular segmentation supports quantitative analysis of the retinal vasculature, yet thin vessels, low contrast, and complex vascular topology remain challenging. We propose EDGE-Net (Enhanced Distribution Gated Eye-vessel Network), which combines the CLARITY preprocessing pipeline, a Dynamic Dual-Stream Attention Block (DDSAB), Multi-Stream Gated Feature Fusion (MSGFF), and topology-aware loss terms based on persistent homology and connectivity regularization. The framework is evaluated on three retinal vessel datasets (DRIVE, CHASE_DB1, and STARE) and two coronary angiography datasets (DCA1 and CHUAC); all hyperparameters are selected on a DRIVE validation split and then fixed for every dataset. EDGE-Net obtains the highest F1 score on all five datasets, ranging from 0.8394 to 0.8456 on the retinal datasets and from 0.7421 to 0.7518 on the coronary datasets, although it does not achieve the highest accuracy or specificity on every dataset. When the same dual-threshold iterative (DTI) post-processing is applied to every method on DRIVE, EDGE-Net obtains the lowest Vessel Connectivity Assessment score (3.31 versus 3.58 for the strongest competitor) and the highest Junction Preservation Rate (0.842 versus 0.812); both differences are significant after Holm correction (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.01  ). A controlled ablation attributes most of the pixel-level gain to DDSAB and MSGFF and most of the junction-preservation gain to the topology loss. Potential downstream uses include anatomically plausible vascular-network analysis; direct clinical benefit is not evaluated in this study.

articles.title: Symmetry-Consistent Attention Supervision for Explainable Multi-label Temporal-Bone CT Assessment.
articles.abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop an explainable deep learning framework for region-wise, multi-label assessment of inner- and middle-ear status on temporal-bone computed tomography (CT). The framework used a ResNet-18 encoder with class-specific attention pooling to predict eight labels representing normal and congenital malformation states of the left and right inner and middle ears. Sparse polygon annotations supervised attention using masked binary cross-entropy, Dice-overlap, and outside-mask penalties. A left-right equivariant consistency regularizer enforced bilateral symmetry under horizontal flipping. The dataset comprised 2399 axial and coronal CT images from 87 patients. Development used fourfold patient-level cross-validation on 35 patients (1018 images), followed by evaluation on a held-out internal test set of 52 patients (1381 images). In cross-validation, the full model achieved a macro-AUC of 0.765 and a macro-F1 of 0.627. On the held-out internal test set, image-level evaluation yielded a macro-AUC of 0.688 and a macro-F1 of 0.572, representing the highest mean performance among the evaluated CNN, vision transformer, and MedViT baselines. Patient-level aggregation further yielded a macro-AUC of 0.716 and a macro-F1 of 0.621. The proposed attention maps were also more side-specific and anatomically concentrated than baseline heatmaps. Attention supervision and bilateral equivariance may improve interpretable temporal-bone CT assessment. Larger external studies and patient-level evaluation are required before clinical deployment.

articles.title: Two-Phase Multimodal Integration of Clinical Text and Imaging for Population-scale Screening of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events.
articles.abstract: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) remain the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential for timely management; however, cardiac risk estimation tools, e.g. PCE and PREVENT, often demonstrate unequal performance across demographic subgroups. Furthermore, confirmatory cardiac imaging modalities (CT, MRI) are costly, invasive, and limited to symptomatic patients. Most predictive studies define outcomes via structured billing codes, which have high error rates and institution-specific variability. We propose a multimodal AI framework enabling large-scale MACE screening using low-cost chest X-rays and clinical text. The approach consists of two phases: (i) an NLP-based pipeline to extract MACE-related outcomes from temporal clinical notes, and (ii) an imaging model trained on these weak labels to estimate MACE risk from chest X-rays, learning latent cardiopulmonary phenotypes denoting cardiovascular risk. We trained these models by automatically curating data from 36,622 patients in the MIMIC-IV-Note and MIMIC-IV-CXR datasets and validating against 250 chart-reviewed patients and 2,152 ED patients from another tertiary care center. Weak MACE labels generated by Mistral-Instruct enabled the imaging model to achieve high performance on internal (AUC = 0.81 [0.78-0.84]) and external (AUC = 0.77 [0.75-0.79]) cohorts, surpassing a fully-supervised baseline. Our findings demonstrate that weakly-supervised learning using large-scale, noisy labels derived from clinical notes substantially improves model generalizability compared with limited manually-annotated datasets. The proposed framework enables population-scale opportunistic cardiovascular screening without requiring dedicated cardiac imaging or extensive manual labeling, discovering subclinical cardiovascular risk signatures embedded within routinely collected clinical data.

articles.title: Category and Modifier Accuracy in a Five-Model Evaluation of Large Language Model Extraction of CAD-RADS 2.0 from Coronary CT Angiography Reports.
articles.abstract: This study evaluates large language model (LLM) extraction of Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) categories from coronary CT angiography (CCTA) reports using a guideline-derived specification and examines instruction-related improvement, repeatability, and the limitations of extracting plaque and ischemia modifiers alongside the category. Five LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, and Copilot) processed 400 deidentified CCTA report entries under unprompted, specified, and repeated-specified conditions. The primary outcome was exact category agreement with a report-derived consensus reference under the specification (n = 400). Secondary outcomes included three-component agreement (n = 396), modifier accuracy, instruction-related changes, and repeatability. Inference used report-text cluster bootstrap and paired or permutation tests with Holm adjustment. For the primary outcome, category accuracy under the specification was 92.8-95.5% (371-382/400); secondary outcomes included run-to-run category agreement of 97.5-98.8%, whereas three-component accuracy was 59.3-81.6% (235-323/396). Among assigned references, plaque accuracy was 79.2-94.0% (236-280/298) and ischemia accuracy 45.1-90.3% (79-158/175). The specification improved category accuracy in four of five models and three-component, plaque, and ischemia accuracy in all five. Models did not differ significantly in category accuracy (Cochran Q = 8.73; adjusted p = 0.077) but differed in three-component accuracy (Q = 116.48; adjusted p < 0.001). Category extraction was accurate under the specification, with improvement in most models and high repeatability. Joint evaluation of category, plaque, and ischemia revealed limitations in modifier extraction. External and prospective validation is needed to develop a reliable clinical tool and establish its value in routine practice.

articles.title: Multifocal isolated bone involvement in Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a 6-week-old infant.
articles.abstract: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) is a rare clonal disorder of dendritic cells with a wide spectrum of clinical and radiologic manifestations. LCH occurs most frequently in infants often manifesting in multisystem or cutaneous disease. Consequently, the isolated multifocal bone involvement seen in this case is an unusual presentation for early infancy. We report a case of a 6-week-old female infant presenting with feeding intolerance and decreased use of the right upper extremity, found to have multifocal lytic skeletal lesions involving the humerus, ribs, calvarium, spine, pelvis, and long bones without clinical or imaging evidence of skin, hepatic, splenic, pulmonary, thymic, gastrointestinal, or central nervous system involvement. Diagnosis was established via CT-guided percutaneous biopsy of a proximal humeral lesion, which confirmed Langerhans cell histiocytosis. This case highlights the imaging features of multifocal osseous LCH in early infancy and demonstrates the safety and diagnostic utility of image-guided long bone biopsy in this vulnerable population. Early recognition and tissue confirmation are essential to avoid misdiagnosis and guide appropriate patient management.

articles.title: Prompt-dependent readability and accuracy of Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 thinking responses to breast imaging questions derived from European Society of Breast Imaging patient recommendations.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Although professional societies provide standardized resources, the reliability of online health content remains inconsistent, particularly as large language models (LLMs) become a growing source of patient information. Therefore, the primary objective of this study was to determine whether patient-focused prompt optimization improves the readability of Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 (GPT-5) Thinking responses compared with standard prompting while evaluating potential changes in expert-rated factual accuracy using educational materials published by the European Society of Breast Imaging (EUSOBI). METHODS: All GPT-5 Thinking outputs were prospectively generated in January 2026. The dataset included frequently asked questions (FAQs) and special information notes (SINs) derived from EUSOBI articles, each submitted under two distinct prompts (standard-Prompt 1 vs. patient-focused-Prompt 2). Readability was quantified using four indices with an averaged composite "reading grade level." Accuracy was scored by two radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. RESULTS: A total of 48 questions (15 FAQs and 33 SIN-derived questions) were each answered under two prompt conditions, yielding 96 responses for analysis. Prompt 2 produced significantly lower readability levels than Prompt 1 across all indices (P < 0.001). These improvements occurred without significant differences in word count (P = 0.12) or sentence count (P = 0.63). The mean accuracy scores remained high and comparable between prompts for all questions (4.54 ± 0.63 vs. 4.52 ± 0.59, P = 0.75). The inter-rater agreement was almost perfect for both the FAQ and SIN-derived question sets (κ = 0.82 and 0.81, respectively). CONCLUSION: Patient-focused prompting substantially reduced the linguistic complexity and reading grade level of GPT-5 Thinking responses without a statistically significant reduction in expert-rated accuracy, demonstrating its ability to produce more accessible breast imaging content, although the resulting grade level remained above widely recommended patient-education thresholds. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: A simple, low-cost prompt modification can substantially improve the readability of LLM-generated patient education content in breast imaging without a measurable reduction in expert-rated accuracy, although further work is needed to confirm this translates into improved patient comprehension.

articles.title: Matching the Tool to the Lesion: First-line Thrombectomy in ICAS-related Vertebrobasilar Occlusion.
GazeCausalNet: Causality-inspired gaze-guided region intervention for breast ultrasound diagnosis.
articles.abstract: Deep learning has advanced breast ultrasound analysis, yet spurious correlations and domain shifts still impede cross-setting generalization. Because most models optimize dataset-dependent associations rather than stable, diagnosis-relevant representations, they may be vulnerable to contextual and acquisition-related factors tied to imaging protocols and acquisition artifacts. To address this, we propose GazeCausalNet, a causality-inspired gaze-guided region intervention framework that uses expert gaze trajectories to identify gaze-attended regions enriched in diagnostic evidence. Based on Linear Optimal Transport (LOT), GazeCausalNet generates smooth and spatially coherent counterfactual-style samples supporting controlled same-class contextual perturbations and opposite-class semantic-transition perturbations. We further introduce counterfactual gradient alignment, comprising background-stability alignment to reduce excessive sensitivity along constructed contextual perturbation directions and semantic-transition alignment to amplify sensitivity to diagnostically meaningful changes. Experiments on public and private breast ultrasound datasets achieve 97.08% and 95.83% AUC, respectively, supporting improved robustness and clinically informed interpretability without claiming formal causal-effect identification.

articles.title: Large language models in radiology: a bibliometric analysis of growth, collaboration, and thematic shifts (November 2022-July 2026).
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To map the development of research on large language models (LLMs) in radiology from November 2022 to July 2026, focusing on publication trends, collaboration patterns, citation distribution, and thematic shifts among Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE)-indexed original research articles. METHODS: A bibliometric analysis was conducted using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Terms related to LLMs and radiology were combined at the topic (title, abstract, and keyword) level, and records retrieved by a complementary title-restricted strategy were screened jointly so that the analytic corpus reflected the union of both strategies. Only original research articles indexed in the SCIE were included. Records were screened independently by three reviewers (Fleiss' κ: 0.67). Publication trends, leading countries, institutions, authors, and journals; international collaboration networks; keyword co-occurrence patterns; citation distributions; and period-stratified thematic shifts were analyzed. Citation concentration was assessed with year-stratified sensitivity analyses, and a post hoc vision-language and foundation model sensitivity search quantified recent literature not captured by the primary strategy. RESULTS: A total of 850 SCIE-indexed articles were included. Annual output increased from 1 article in 2022 to 380 in 2025 (2026 partial). The dataset accumulated 10,767 citations (mean 12.67 per article; Hirsch index 48), but impact was concentrated: The 10% most cited articles accounted for 63.8% of all citations, and 28.5% of articles were uncited (8.0% excluding the partial 2026 window). The United States was the most productive country and the most connected hub of international collaboration by total link strength and betweenness centrality, followed by China, Germany, and Türkiye. Publications concentrated in a small number of high-impact journals, led by Radiology. Keyword and period-stratified analyses showed a shift from early ChatGPT-centered feasibility studies toward general LLM and modality-specific evaluation, with keyword-level signals of an emerging multimodal direction. CONCLUSION: Research on LLMs in the SCIE-indexed radiology literature has expanded rapidly since 2022. Keyword patterns suggest a gradual shift from exploratory, text-only applications toward clinically oriented evaluation, with early keyword-level signals of a multimodal direction, although methodological heterogeneity and the absence of standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks remain the main barriers to clinical adoption. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: By quantifying where, by whom, and on which themes LLM research in radiology is produced, this analysis helps radiologists, researchers, and funders identify under-studied modalities and applications, locate established collaboration networks, and direct future work toward the standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks the field currently lacks.
